question: A child with ANA-positive oligoarticular JIA should be referred for slit-lamp ophthalmological screening even if they have no eye symptoms or visual complaints.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is a critical safety point. Uveitis in oligoarticular JIA does not cause red eye or pain; the child will not complain. The only way to detect it early enough to prevent vision loss is mandatory periodic slit-lamp examination regardless of symptoms.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Uveitis in ANA-positive oligoarticular JIA is characteristically asymptomatic — no redness, no pain, no photophobia — yet can progress to band keratopathy and blindness if undetected. Regular slit-lamp screening (every 3–6 months) is mandatory.
